name: Machine Chest Press

startingWeightKg.note: Machine stacks differ between brands, so ignore the number on other machines. Week 1: pick a weight you can press for 12 clean reps with about 3 reps left in the tank. Log the pin number and the seat setting in the app.

setup: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest (around nipple height), not your neck.
If the machine has a foot lever or start-position adjuster, set the handles so you feel a light stretch across your chest at the start, not a painful pull at the front of the shoulder.
Sit tall with your back and head on the pad, feet flat and a bit wider than hips.
Grip the horizontal handles (palms down) or the vertical ones (palms facing in, easier on the shoulders) with your wrists stacked straight over your forearms.
Before the first rep, pull your shoulder blades slightly back and down into the pad.
cues: Chest up, shoulder blades in the pad
Push the handles away, not up
Elbows about 45-60 degrees from your body, not flared straight out
Stop just short of locking out
2-3 seconds back, feel the stretch
mistakes: Seat too low so you press upward like a shoulder press
Shoulders rolling forward off the pad at the end of each rep
Letting the stack slam between reps
Arching the lower back off the pad to move more weight
Bouncing out of the bottom with no control
breathing: Breathe in as the handles come back toward you, exhale steadily as you press them away. Don't hold your breath for the whole set.
safety: The best first chest exercise for a beginner: the path is fixed, you can't drop anything and you don't need a spotter. If the front of a shoulder pinches, shorten the range at the start (move the handle adjuster forward) and use the neutral (palms-in) handles. Keep your feet planted so your hips stay on the seat.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press

startingWeightKg.note: Per dumbbell. Start at 10 kg per hand in week 1 to learn getting the dumbbells into position safely, then move up. Go up to the next dumbbell pair available (usually +2 or +2.5 kg per hand). If that jump is too big, add reps first (double progression).

setup: Set an adjustable bench flat. Put the dumbbells on the floor at the end of the bench.
Sit on the end of the bench with a dumbbell standing upright on each thigh, close to your knees.
Lie back and use your knees to 'kick' the dumbbells up as your back reaches the bench, so they arrive over your chest with straight arms.
Feet flat on the floor, shoulder blades pulled back and down, a small natural arch in the lower back with your butt on the bench.
Start with the dumbbells over your lower chest, palms facing your feet or turned slightly in.
cues: Shoulder blades pinched, chest proud
Lower to the sides of your chest, elbows about 45 degrees
Forearms vertical under the dumbbells
Press up and slightly together
Control the way down for 2-3 seconds
mistakes: Flaring elbows to 90 degrees (stresses the shoulder)
Dropping the dumbbells to the side when finished instead of bringing them to your chest and sitting up
Going too deep with a big stretch in week 1
Clanking the dumbbells together at the top
Hips lifting off the bench
breathing: Breathe in and brace on the way down, exhale as you press up.
safety: Finishing the set safely: bring the dumbbells to your chest, tuck your knees up, and rock up to sitting with the dumbbells on your thighs. Don't drop them out wide. Dumbbells are friendlier on the shoulders than a barbell because your hands can find a comfortable path, and if you fail a rep you can lower them to the floor without getting stuck.

startingWeightKg.note: Per dumbbell; about 20% lighter than your flat dumbbell press. Go up to the next dumbbell pair available (usually +2 or +2.5 kg per hand). If that jump is too big, add reps first (double progression).

setup: Set the bench back to a low incline, about 30 degrees (usually the 2nd or 3rd notch). Steeper turns it into a shoulder press.
Set the seat one notch up if it adjusts, so you don't slide down.
Sit with the dumbbells on your thighs, lie back and kick them up one at a time or together to the top of your chest.
Feet flat, shoulder blades back and down against the pad, chest up.
cues: Low incline, chest up to the ceiling
Lower to your upper chest, elbows slightly tucked
Press up and slightly in, over your collarbones
Slow on the way down
mistakes: Bench too steep (45 degrees or more), so mostly shoulders work
Shoulders shrugging up toward the ears
Lowering the dumbbells too far down behind the body
Bouncing at the bottom
breathing: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you press up.
safety: Keep the range comfortable for the shoulders: stop when your elbows are about level with the bench, or slightly below. Use the same safe exit as on the flat press: dumbbells to your chest, then sit up.

startingWeightKg.note: TOTAL load including the bar. Smith bars weigh about 7-20 kg depending on the model (some are counterbalanced), so ask staff or log 'bar + plates'. Set the safety stops just below where the bar touches your chest. They catch the bar if you fail a rep.
Lie down, eyes roughly under the bar, feet flat. Grip a little wider than shoulder width.
Pinch your shoulder blades back and down, then twist the bar to unhook it (practice the hook/unhook with the empty bar first).

Bar to the lower chest
Elbows tucked about 45 degrees
Push your back into the bench
Twist to rack at the top

Not setting the safety stops
Bouncing the bar off the chest
Forgetting to twist and re-hook, then letting go
breathing: Inhale and brace before you lower the bar, exhale through the hardest part of the press.
safety: A good 'barbell-like' option without a spotter: set the safety stops every time and you can't get pinned. The fixed path is fine for building muscle. Keep the reps controlled.

Position the bench so the bar comes down to your upper chest, just below your collarbones.
Set the safety stops just below that touch point.
Grip slightly wider than shoulder width, pinch the shoulder blades back and down, feet flat, then twist to unhook.
cues: Bar to your upper chest
Elbows slightly under the bar, not flared
Chest up, shoulders down
Smooth press, twist to rack

Bar landing on your neck or face because the bench is in the wrong spot
Shoulders shrugged up
Half reps with too much weight
breathing: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you press.

name: Barbell Bench Press

startingWeightKg.note: TOTAL including a 20 kg Olympic bar (some gym bars are lighter, so check). First session: empty bar only, to practise unracking and the bar path. Then add 2.5-5 kg per side each session until 12 reps leave about 3 in the tank (often 30-40 kg total after a month of Smith/dumbbell pressing), then add 1.25-2.5 kg per side when you hit the top of the rep range. ONLY possible on a bench with built-in uprights AND safety arms/pins, or with a spotter. The gym equipment list doesn't confirm one; if there isn't one, the app should swap to smith_machine_bench_press.

setup: REQUIRES a bench-press bench with uprights (rack). If the gym doesn't have one, do the Smith machine bench press instead. Lie down with your eyes directly under the bar.
Grip so that your forearms are vertical when the bar touches your chest (usually a bit wider than shoulder width, index fingers around the rings).
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and down, feet flat and planted, slight arch, butt stays on the bench.
Unrack with straight arms and move the bar over your shoulders before starting.
Set the safety arms/pins just below chest height if the station has them. If it doesn't, only bench with a spotter standing behind you. Never bench a barbell alone without safeties.

Bar to the lower chest / nipple line
Elbows about 45-70 degrees
Drive your feet into the floor
Press up and slightly back, finish over your shoulders

Elbows flared to 90 degrees
Wrists bent backwards
Butt lifting off the bench
Benching alone without a spotter or safety pins
breathing: Breathe in and brace before you lower the bar, then exhale steadily as you press up. Avoid long breath-holds, especially if you have (or don't know your) blood pressure.
safety: Highest-skill press in this list, so it's kept as a later option (month 2+). Never bench a barbell alone without safety pins or a spotter. If no safeties or spotter are available, use the Smith machine or dumbbells instead. A heavier lifter's bigger chest means a shorter bar path, which is fine; don't force extra depth.

Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs.

Hold a dumbbell vertically at your chest (or arms out front for bodyweight).
If touching the bench is too deep at first, only squat until your butt lightly brushes it, or use leg_press until it feels better. Do NOT stack loose plates on the bench to sit on - they can slide.
cues: Reach your hips back to the bench
Touch softly - do not crash down
Stay tight, pause 1 second
Drive up through mid-foot, chest up
mistakes: Plopping down and relaxing on the bench
Rocking forward to stand up
Knees collapsing inward
Bench too far away so you have to fall back
breathing: Inhale and brace before you sit back; exhale as you stand up.
safety: Great first squat for a heavier beginner: the bench sets a safe depth and gives confidence. Make sure the bench is stable and will not tip or slide; never sit back onto the end of a bench that can flip.

video.title: How To: Dumbbell Goblet Box Squat

name: Smith Machine Squat

startingWeightKg.note: TOTAL including the Smith bar (bars are often 15-20 kg, some counter-balanced to less - ask staff or treat the bar as ~15 kg). First session: empty bar for 2 sets to learn the groove, then add 2.5-5 kg per side.

setup: Set the bar hooks at about upper-chest/shoulder height so you can unrack with a small knee bend.
Set the safety stops just below your lowest squat depth (try the depth with an empty bar first).
Step under the bar; rest it on the meaty upper back (traps), NOT the neck. Hands just outside shoulders.
Feet shoulder-width, slightly IN FRONT of the bar (about a half foot-length) so you can sit down and back, toes slightly out.
Stand up, twist the bar to unhook it.
cues: Brace your belly like you are about to be poked
Sit down and slightly back
Knees out, whole foot on the floor
Thighs to about parallel (or a bench-safe depth)
Drive up, twist to rack when done
mistakes: Feet directly under the bar (puts stress on knees/lower back)
Bar on the neck
Forgetting to set the safeties
Bouncing at the bottom
Knees caving in
breathing: Deep breath and brace at the top, hold through the descent, exhale through pursed lips as you pass the hardest part on the way up.
safety: The fixed path and safety stops make this safer than a free barbell squat for a solo beginner - you can just twist to rack at any point. Keep depth to what you control with a flat back. Wrap a towel around the bar if it digs in.

video.title: Smith machine squats proper form

name: Supported Split Squat

startingWeightKg.note: Start bodyweight, holding onto a support with one or both hands. When 3x12 per leg is easy, hold one light dumbbell in the hand on the same side as the BACK leg while the other hand keeps holding the support.

setup: Stand beside a stable support: the locked Smith machine bar set at waist/chest height, the Smith frame, or an adjustable bench upright.
Take a long step: one foot forward, the other back on the ball of the foot, feet hip-width apart (like on train tracks, not a tightrope).
Hold the support lightly - use it for balance, not to pull yourself up.
Most weight goes on the FRONT foot.
cues: Drop the back knee straight down
Front heel stays heavy
Torso tall, slight forward lean is OK
Push through the front foot to rise
Finish all reps on one side, then switch
mistakes: Stance too narrow (wobbly)
Pushing off the back foot instead of the front
Front heel lifting
Banging the back knee on the floor
breathing: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you push up.
safety: Holding a support removes the balance problem that makes lunges hard for heavier beginners. Go only as low as is comfortable for the knees - the back knee does not need to touch the floor. Count reps per leg.

video.title: Beginner's Guide: Split Squat

name: Dumbbell Step-Up (Low Step)

startingWeightKg.note: Per hand. Start bodyweight on a LOW step; add 5-8 kg dumbbells only when 10 smooth reps per leg feel easy.

setup: Use the lowest stable step the gym has (an aerobic step or low box about 25-35 cm, if there is one - ask staff). A standard flat bench is about 43-45 cm, which is high for a 170 cm beginner: if that is the only option, use bodyweight only and hold a support (for example the Smith machine frame next to the bench) with one hand. Never stack loose plates to make a step.
Make sure the bench/step is stable and dry (wipe off sweat).
Place the WHOLE working foot on the step.
Hold dumbbells at your sides (or nothing for bodyweight).
cues: Lean slightly forward over the front foot
Drive through the heel of the top foot
Do not push off with the bottom foot
Stand tall at the top, then step down slowly
All reps one leg, then switch
mistakes: Step too high for your current strength
Bouncing off the back foot
Front knee caving inward
Dropping down fast on the way down
breathing: Exhale as you step up, inhale as you lower down.
safety: Lower step height = less knee stress and easier balance. Never use a bench that wobbles, and step down with control. Skip load until balance is solid.

video.title: Dumbbell Step Ups - Leg Exercise - Bodybuilding.com

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift

startingWeightKg.note: Per dumbbell. Learn the hinge first with light dumbbells (8-10 kg each); a deep hamstring stretch with a flat back matters more than load.

setup: Stand tall, feet hip-width, a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing you.
Unlock the knees slightly (soft knees) and keep them there the whole set.
Shoulders back and down, chest proud, look at the floor about 2 m ahead.
cues: Push your hips back like closing a car door with your butt
Dumbbells slide down your thighs
Flat back - stop when hamstrings are tight (around mid-shin)
Squeeze glutes to stand up tall
Do not lean back at the top
mistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach lower
Turning it into a squat (bending knees too much)
Dumbbells drifting away from the legs
Hyper-extending/leaning back at the top
breathing: Inhale and brace at the top, hold as you hinge down, exhale as you stand up.
safety: Range of motion ends where your back would start to round - for most beginners that is around the knees to mid-shin. Move slowly. If your lower back (not hamstrings) feels it, reduce weight and range. Dry hands - sweaty grip is a real issue in Accra heat.

video.title: Dumbbell Romanian (RDL) Deadlift |TECHNIQUE for Beginners

name: Smith Machine Hip Thrust

startingWeightKg.note: TOTAL including the Smith bar. Start with the bar only to learn the position; glutes are strong, so you can usually add 5-10 kg per session early on. A free barbell rolled over the hips works the same way once confident.

setup: Put a flat bench crosswise inside the Smith machine, against something solid so it cannot slide.
Sit on the floor with your upper back (bottom of the shoulder blades) against the bench edge.
Set the bar at a height where it rests on your hip crease when you are sitting; wrap a folded towel or bar pad around the bar.
Feet flat, about shoulder-width; at the top your shins should be vertical (adjust feet forward/back).
Set the Smith safety stops just below the bar's lowest point (butt almost on the floor) so the bar can never pin you.
Hold the bar with both hands, push up and twist to unhook.
cues: Chin tucked, eyes forward (not at the ceiling)
Drive through the heels
Ribs down - tuck the pelvis at the top
Squeeze glutes hard for 1 second
Lower until butt nearly touches the floor
mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of extending the hips
Feet too close (quads take over) or too far (hamstrings cramp)
Bench sliding away
No pad - bar bruising hips
breathing: Inhale at the bottom, exhale as you thrust up and squeeze.
safety: Very back-friendly glute builder. Always use padding on the bar and set the safety stops. Twist to re-rack at the top when done. On a humid day, put a towel on the bench edge so your sweaty back does not slide.

video.title: How to: Smith Machine Glute Bridge (Hip Thrust) | Grow Bigger Glutes w/ Minimal Setup

name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust

startingWeightKg.note: One dumbbell across the hips. Start with a set of 10-15 bodyweight reps. When the heaviest dumbbell becomes easy for 15, move to smith_machine_hip_thrust.

setup: Sit on the floor with your upper back against the long side of a flat bench (bench against a wall or rack so it cannot slide).
Place one dumbbell horizontally across your hip crease with a towel underneath; hold both ends.
Feet flat, shoulder-width, knees bent so shins are vertical at the top.
cues: Chin tucked, ribs down
Drive through the heels
Squeeze glutes hard at the top - body flat like a table
Pause 1 second, lower with control
mistakes: Overarching the lower back at the top
Letting the dumbbell roll toward the stomach
Pushing through the toes
Rushing the reps
breathing: Inhale at the bottom, exhale as you drive up.
safety: Easy to set up and to get out of: just roll the dumbbell off to the side. Towel under the dumbbell for comfort; towel on the bench for a sweaty back.

video.title: Dumbbell Hip Thrust (FULL TUTORIAL) - Glute Exercises for Beginners

name: Glute Bridge
setup: Lie on your back on a mat if the gym has one (or a towel on a clean floor), knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart about 20-30 cm from your butt.
Arms flat at your sides, palms down.
Optional progression: rest a dumbbell on your hips (hold the ends) once 20 reps feel easy.
cues: Flatten your lower back to the floor first
Push through the heels
Squeeze glutes to lift hips into a straight line
Hold 2 seconds at the top
Lower slowly
mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top
Pushing through the toes
Knees falling in or out
Feet too far away (hamstrings cramp)
breathing: Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
safety: Excellent glute warm-up before leg day and a safe back-friendly exercise. Also good as a warm-up set before hip thrusts.

video.title: How to Perform the Perfect Glute Bridge

name: Cable Glute Kickback (Ankle Strap)

startingWeightKg.note: Per leg. Very light at first - this is a squeeze exercise, not a heavy one.

setup: NOTE (equipment uncertain): this needs an ankle cuff/strap for the cable machine. The 'Ankle machine' on the gym list turned out to be a calf raise machine, so an ankle strap is not confirmed. Ask gym staff; if there is no strap, do glute_bridge or dumbbell_hip_thrust instead.
Set the pulley to the lowest position and clip the ankle strap on.
Wrap the strap around the working ankle; face the machine and hold the frame with both hands.
Step back so there is tension, stand on the non-working leg with a soft knee and lean the torso slightly forward.
cues: Kick the leg back and slightly out
Squeeze the glute at the end - pause 1 second
Do not arch your lower back to get higher
Return slowly, keep tension
All reps one leg, then switch
mistakes: Swinging with momentum
Arching the lower back
Too much weight so the torso twists
Standing leg locked straight
breathing: Exhale as you kick back, inhale as you return.
safety: Low spinal load. Holding the frame removes the balance challenge. Use light weight and control. Low priority accessory: only add if time allows within a 45-60 min session.

video.title: How To Cable Kickback (Glute Kickback Form Tutorial)

name: Leg Press Calf Raise

startingWeightKg.note: Weight ADDED to the sled. Usually done right after leg press - simply strip some plates off. Pick a load you can do 15 full-range reps with.

setup: Sit in the leg press as normal; place only the BALLS of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform, hip-width.
Press the sled up with legs straight but knees NOT hard-locked (a tiny bend).
KEEP THE SAFETY HANDLES ENGAGED if your machine allows calf raises with them on; otherwise keep the load modest.
cues: Let the heels go back for a deep stretch - pause 1-2 s
Push through the big toe to point the feet
Squeeze at the top 1 second
Slow and full range, no bouncing
mistakes: Bouncing at the bottom
Bending the knees to help
Tiny partial reps
Feet too high so they slip
breathing: Breathe steadily: exhale as you press, inhale as you lower.
safety: Main risk is the feet slipping off the platform with the sled above you. Use dry shoes, wipe sweat off the platform, keep the whole ball of each foot (not just the toes) on the platform and do not go so heavy that you cannot control the bottom. Re-engage the safety handles straight after the last rep before taking your feet off.

video.title: Leg Press Calves

name: Smith Machine Calf Raise

startingWeightKg.note: TOTAL including the Smith bar. Remember you are also lifting your own 95 kg - start with bar only and focus on full range.

setup: Place a flat, stable 20 kg plate (or a low step) under the bar to stand on so the heels can drop below the toes.
Set the bar at shoulder height; bar on the upper back as for the Smith squat.
Stand with the balls of your feet on the edge of the plate, heels hanging off, legs straight with a soft knee.
Twist to unrack; set the safety stops just below the bar position.
cues: Heels drop low - pause 1-2 s in the stretch
Rise up as high as possible onto the big toe
Squeeze 1 s at the top
Knees stay still
mistakes: Bouncing
Short range
Plate wobbling or sliding
Bending knees to push
breathing: Exhale on the way up, inhale on the way down.
safety: The Smith machine handles balance. Make sure the plate you stand on cannot slide (rubber floor, flat plate). If balancing is awkward, use leg_press_calf_raise instead.

video.title: Smith Machine Calves

name: Dumbbell Standing Calf Raise

startingWeightKg.note: Two-leg version: start with bodyweight or one dumbbell held in one hand (other hand on a support). Your 95 kg bodyweight already loads the calves well. Progress to single-leg holding one dumbbell.

setup: Stand on a flat 20 kg plate or a low step with the balls of your feet on the edge, heels free.
Hold a dumbbell in one hand; hold a rack, Smith frame or wall with the other for balance.
Legs straight with a soft knee.
cues: Slow stretch at the bottom - pause
Rise high onto the big toe
Squeeze at the top
Do not bounce
mistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom
Rolling out onto the little toe
Short range
Leaning heavily on the support
breathing: Exhale up, inhale down.
safety: Low-risk calf option that needs almost no setup. Make sure the plate/step does not slide.

video.title: Standing Dumbbell Calf Raises - Calf Exercise - Bodybuilding.com

name: Dead Bug
setup: Lie on your back on a mat if the gym has one (or a towel on a clean floor). Arms straight up toward the ceiling.
Lift knees above hips, bent 90 degrees (tabletop).
Press your lower back gently into the floor and keep it there.
Reps are counted per side (left arm/right leg = 1).
cues: Lower back stays glued to the floor
Slowly lower opposite arm and leg
Exhale fully as you reach
Only go as low as you can keep the back flat
Switch sides with control
mistakes: Lower back arching off the floor
Moving too fast
Holding the breath
Moving same-side arm and leg
breathing: Exhale slowly as the arm and leg extend, inhale as they return.
safety: One of the safest core exercises - no spine flexion and no load. Easier version: keep the knee bent and just tap the heel to the floor.

video.title: How to Do a Dead Bug: A Guide from Physical Therapists

name: Front Plank
setup: Forearms on the floor (on a mat or towel if available), elbows under the shoulders.
Legs straight back, toes on the floor, feet hip-width.
If this is too hard right now, start with incline_plank (hands/forearms on a bench) or on the knees.
cues: Body straight from head to heels
Squeeze glutes and pull belly button in
Push the floor away with the forearms
Breathe - do not hold your breath
Stop when the hips sag
mistakes: Hips sagging toward the floor
Butt piked up high
Holding the breath
Looking up and straining the neck
breathing: Short, steady breaths through the nose/mouth while keeping the belly braced.
safety: For a 95 kg beginner a full plank is genuinely hard; good form for 20 s beats sagging for 60 s. Stop the set the moment the lower back aches. Progress time by 5 s per week up to ~45-60 s.

video.title: How To Plank (Proper Form | Cues | Progressions)

name: Incline Plank (Hands on Bench)
setup: Use a flat bench (or an adjustable bench at its flat setting) that is stable.
Place forearms (or straight arms) on the bench, elbows under shoulders.
Walk your feet back until your body is in a straight line.
The higher the support, the easier: Smith bar locked at hip height is an even easier version.
cues: Straight line head to heels
Squeeze glutes
Ribs down, belly braced
Breathe steadily
mistakes: Hips sagging
Shrugging the shoulders to the ears
Holding breath
breathing: Steady short breaths while keeping the brace.
safety: The ideal starting plank for a heavier beginner - less load on shoulders and lower back. When 3 x 45 s is easy, move to the floor plank.

video.title: How to do an Incline Plank - Strength Exercises - Wellen

name: Side Plank
setup: Lie on your side on a mat if the gym has one (or a towel on a clean floor), elbow directly under the shoulder.
BEGINNER VERSION: knees bent 90 degrees behind you, lift from the knees.
Full version: legs straight and stacked (or top foot in front for balance).
Time is per side.
cues: Lift hips so the body is a straight line
Push the floor away with the elbow
Do not let the hips drop or roll back
Breathe
mistakes: Hips sagging
Body rolling forward or back
Elbow not under the shoulder
Holding breath
breathing: Steady breathing while braced.
safety: Start with the bent-knee version - the straight-leg version puts a lot of load on the shoulder for a 95 kg lifter. Stop if the shoulder hurts. Spine-friendly oblique work (McGill "big three" style).

video.title: How to do a Side Plank  | Proper Form & Technique | NASM

name: Kneeling Cable Crunch

startingWeightKg.note: Stack weights vary. Pick a weight you can crunch 12-15 times while feeling the abs, not the arms or hips.

setup: Attach the rope to the HIGH pulley.
Hold the rope ends beside your face/ears and kneel down facing the machine, about an arm length away (a folded towel or mat under the knees).
Hips stay high (do not sit on your heels).
cues: Curl your ribs down toward your hips
Elbows go toward the thighs
Round your back - it is a crunch
Hips stay still, do not sit back
Slowly return to a stretch
mistakes: Sitting back on the heels / pulling with the hips
Pulling with the arms
Using too much weight
Keeping the back flat (no crunch)
breathing: Exhale hard as you crunch down, inhale as you rise.
safety: Weighted ab exercise that is easy to load progressively. Keep the movement in the spine and hips still; do not yank the weight.

video.title: Cable Crunch - Abs / Core Exercise - Bodybuilding.com

name: Pallof Press

startingWeightKg.note: Light. Choose a weight that tries to twist you but you can resist for 10 slow reps per side.

setup: Set a single handle at chest height on the cable machine.
Stand side-on to the machine, hold the handle with both hands at your chest.
Step sideways 2-3 steps away so the cable has tension; feet shoulder-width, soft knees.
Reps are per side - turn around and repeat.
cues: Press the handle straight out from your chest
Do not let the cable twist you
Hold 2 seconds with arms straight
Glutes and abs tight
Bring it back slowly
mistakes: Rotating toward the machine
Leaning away from the cable
Too heavy
Shrugging
breathing: Exhale as you press out, breathe steadily during the hold, inhale as you bring it back.
safety: Anti-rotation core training with no spine bending - very back-friendly and well suited to beginners.

video.title: How To Perform The Pallof Press Exercise For Less Lower Back Pain

name: Cable Woodchop (High to Low)

startingWeightKg.note: Light and controlled. This is a core exercise, not an arm one.

setup: Set a single handle at the HIGH pulley.
Stand side-on, grab the handle with both hands, arms straight above the shoulder nearest the machine.
Step away so there is tension; feet wider than shoulders, soft knees.
Reps per side.
cues: Pull diagonally across your body to the opposite hip
Turn the trunk and pivot the back foot
Arms stay long - the core does the work
Return slowly and under control
mistakes: Pulling with the arms only
Twisting from the lower back without pivoting hips/foot
Going too heavy and jerking
Rushing back up
breathing: Exhale as you chop down, inhale as you return.
safety: Pivot the back foot so the hips turn with the shoulders - this protects the lower back. Keep the load light. If any back discomfort, swap for pallof_press.

video.title: How To: Oblique Twist "Wood Chopper" (LF CAble)

name: Bench Leg Raise (Bent-Knee)
setup: Lie on your back on a flat bench, butt near the end, legs off the end.
Hold the bench behind your head (or the sides) for support.
BEGINNER VERSION: bend the knees 90 degrees; straight legs make it much harder.
cues: Press the lower back into the bench
Bring the knees toward the chest
Curl the hips up slightly at the top
Lower slowly - stop before the back arches
mistakes: Lower back arching off the bench as the legs drop
Swinging the legs
Straight legs before you are ready
Only moving the hip flexors (no pelvic curl)
breathing: Exhale as the knees come up, inhale as they lower.
safety: Long levers stress the lower back - stay with bent knees until 3x15 is easy. If the lower back aches, shorten the range or swap for dead_bug. Also works the hip flexors.

video.title: How To: Lying Leg Raise On Bench

name: Easy Cardio (Bike or Treadmill)
setup: Use whichever is free: an upright bike or a treadmill.
Bike: set the seat so your knee is only slightly bent (about 25-35 degrees) when the pedal is at the bottom; resistance low (level 2-4 of most consoles).

Treadmill: clip the safety key to your shirt, stand on the side rails, start the belt at its slowest speed (about 1-2 km/h), step on while holding the rails lightly, then raise to 4.5-5 km/h, incline 0-2%, and let go of the rails.
Put your water bottle and towel within reach; Legon afternoons are hot, so start sipping now.
Use the same machine at the end of the session for a 3-5 minute easy cool-down walk/ride.
cues: Easy pace - you could hold a full conversation (effort 3/10).
Last minute: pick it up slightly until you feel warm and lightly sweaty.
Shoulders relaxed, breathe through your nose if you can.
mistakes: Going hard here and tiring yourself out before lifting.
Skipping it because you walked to the gym - a few minutes on the machine still raises muscle and joint temperature.
Holding the treadmill rails with straight arms.
breathing: Relaxed, steady breathing. If you cannot speak in full sentences, slow down.
safety: Five minutes of low-intensity cardio warms knees, hips and ankles before loading them - important at 95 kg. In the heat, keep it easy; you will sweat early. Stop and tell staff if you feel dizzy, chest pain or unusually short of breath.

video.title: Correct Stationary Bike Set Up

name: Stationary Bike - Steady State (Zone 2)
setup: Seat height: stand next to the bike, set the seat roughly level with your hip bone. Sit, put your heel on the pedal at the very bottom - your leg should be almost straight. Pedalling on the balls of your feet then gives a small knee bend.
Seat fore/aft (if adjustable): with pedals level, your front knee should sit roughly over the pedal, not far in front of it.
Handlebars at seat height or a bit higher so you sit upright - more comfortable for the lower back and belly.
Choose 'manual' mode. Start at a low resistance level and adjust until you reach the target effort.
Have water and a towel ready; position near a fan if there is one.
cues: Effort 5-6/10: you can talk in short sentences but not sing.
Smooth circles - push down and pull back through the bottom.
Cadence around 70-90 RPM; add resistance rather than spinning like crazy.
Knees track straight over your feet, not caving in.
Relax your grip and shoulders.
mistakes: Seat too low (knees come up high and hurt at the front) or too high (hips rock side to side).
Resistance so low you just spin with no effort - or so high you grind at 40 RPM.
Hunching over the handlebars and putting weight on the hands.
Starting with 40+ minutes in week one and dreading the next session.
breathing: Steady, rhythmic breathing; you should be able to say a sentence. If you are gasping, lower resistance.
safety: The best low-impact cardio for a 95 kg beginner - no pounding on knees or ankles. Approx. heart rate target for a 20-something: about 120-140 bpm (roughly 60-70% of max) - the 'talk test' works just as well. Do it AFTER lifting (or on non-lifting days) so it doesn't tire your legs before squats/presses. Start with 10-15 min and build to 20-30 min. In hot, humid weather drink before you're thirsty; stop if dizzy or nauseous.

video.title: Correct Stationary Bike Set Up

name: Treadmill Incline Walk
setup: Check the treadmill is working and clip the safety key/cord to your shirt.
Stand on the side rails, start the belt at its slowest speed (about 1-2 km/h) at 0% incline, then step on while holding the rails lightly.
Raise speed to 4.5-5.0 km/h first, then raise incline gradually to 4-6% for the first sessions.
Progress over weeks: add incline 1-2% at a time up to ~10-12%, or add minutes (15 -> 20 -> 30). Keep speed a walking pace (4.5-5.5 km/h).
Wear proper trainers (not slides/sandals) and keep water nearby.
cues: Hands OFF the rails - arms swing naturally.
Stand tall, slight forward lean from the ankles, not bending at the waist.
Full foot contact: heel lands, push through the whole foot.
Effort 5-6/10 - breathing harder but able to talk.
Short, quick steps if your calves or shins burn.
mistakes: Gripping the handrails and leaning back - this cuts the work dramatically and wrecks posture.
Cranking the incline to 15% in week one and getting shin or calf pain.
Walking too fast and starting to jog uphill.
Stepping off a moving belt to grab water.
breathing: Breathe steadily through nose and mouth; if you can't talk, drop the incline 1-2% first, then speed.
safety: Excellent for a 95 kg beginner: burns lots of calories with far less joint impact than running. Build incline slowly because calves, Achilles and shins need time to adapt. Most gym treadmills are rated for 130-150 kg, so you're fine. To stop: lower speed, then lower incline, then step onto the side rails. Hot gym = higher heart rate; that's normal, but slow down if dizzy. Do after lifting or on rest days.

video.title: How To: Incline Treadmill Walk (12-3-30 Workout)

name: Treadmill Brisk Walk
setup: Clip the safety key to your clothing.
Stand on the side rails, start the belt at its slowest speed (about 1-2 km/h), step on, then increase to a brisk pace of about 5.0-6.0 km/h.
Incline 1% (simulates outdoor walking); increase to 2-3% later if it feels too easy.
Use it as a cool-down (5 min at an easier 4-4.5 km/h) or as a standalone 15-30 min session on off days.
cues: Walk like you're late for a lecture - purposeful, not a jog.
Arms bent and swinging, hands off the rails.
Eyes forward, not down at your feet.
Effort 4-5/10 - slightly out of breath but chatting is easy.
mistakes: Holding the rails.
Over-striding (big heel-first lunges) - take shorter, quicker steps.
Looking down at your phone the whole time and drifting to the back of the belt.
breathing: Easy rhythmic breathing; you should be able to talk.
safety: The gentlest cardio option - good for the very first weeks, recovery days or when knees/shins feel tired. Brisk walking is a proven fat-loss tool when paired with a calorie deficit. Hydrate in the heat and stop if light-headed.

video.title: How to Walk Properly on a Treadmill to Reduce Pain | Expert Tips for Comfort and Relief

name: Stationary Bike Intervals (Beginner)
setup: Set the bike up exactly as for steady state (heel on pedal at bottom = almost straight leg).
Warm up 3-4 minutes easy.
Then repeat: 30 seconds HARD (raise resistance 2-4 levels, effort 7-8/10) + 90 seconds EASY (back to warm-up resistance, effort 3/10).
Week 1-2 of using intervals: 4 rounds. Build to 6-8 rounds over a month.
Finish with 2-3 minutes easy spinning. Total about 15 minutes.
cues: Hard parts: stay seated, push with resistance - don't flail at max RPM.
Hard = breathing heavily, can only say a word or two.
Easy parts: really ease off so you recover.
Keep knees tracking over toes, upper body still.
mistakes: Doing intervals in the first 3-4 weeks before building a base with steady rides.
All-out sprints with no resistance (pedals spin away and hips bounce).
Skipping the warm-up or cool-down.
Doing intervals right before a leg day - it will hurt your squats/leg press.
breathing: Breathe hard but controlled during efforts; slow, deep breaths during the 90-second easy recovery.
safety: Use only after 3-4 weeks of steady cardio and only 1x per week (max 2) - for a 95 kg beginner who lifts 3x/week, more high-intensity work just adds fatigue. Bike is chosen over treadmill sprints because there's no impact. In the heat, keep the efforts at 7-8/10, not 10/10. Stop immediately if chest pain, dizziness or nausea. If you have any heart/blood-pressure condition, check with a doctor before intervals.

video.title: How To Do A HIIT On An Exercise Bike | The Body Coach
video.channel: The Body Coach TV by Joe Wicks

name: Arm Circles
setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, plenty of space around you.
Arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height.
Do 10-15 small circles forward, growing to big circles, then 10-15 backward.
cues: Start small, finish big.
Keep your ribs down - don't arch your back.
Shoulders away from ears.
Smooth, controlled, not whipping.
mistakes: Swinging wildly or fast enough to jerk the shoulder.
Shrugging the shoulders up.
Only going forward - do both directions.
breathing: Breathe normally.
safety: Gentle way to warm the shoulders before push or pull days. If any position pinches, make the circles smaller.

video.title: Arm Circles Exercise

name: Towel Shoulder Pass-Through
setup: Use a LONG towel (bath-towel size, roughly 1.2-1.5 m) or a long strap/belt - a small hand towel is too short for your shoulder width. Hold it pulled tight in front of your hips with a VERY wide grip - near the ends.
Do NOT use a barbell or the 20 kg Olympic bar for this - it's too heavy and stiff for a beginner's shoulders.
Stand tall, glutes squeezed lightly, ribs down.
cues: Keep the towel tight and arms straight.
Lift slowly up over your head and back behind you as far as is comfortable, then return.
If you need to bend the elbows or feel a pinch, widen your grip.
Ribs down - don't arch your lower back to get the towel back.
mistakes: Grip too narrow, forcing the shoulders.
Arching the lower back or poking the head forward.
Rushing through reps.
breathing: Inhale as the towel goes up, exhale as it comes back down.
safety: Safe, gradual shoulder opener before pressing and lat pulldowns. A towel lets you go as wide as you need. Stop if you feel pain (stretch is fine, pinch/pain is not). Skip if you've ever dislocated a shoulder.

video.title: Shoulder Pass Through

name: Scapular Wall Slides
setup: Find a clear wall (or a smooth pillar).
Stand with your back against the wall, feet about a foot (30 cm) in front of it, knees soft.
Easiest version for beginners: face the wall and put your forearms on it in a 'goalpost' shape.
Back-to-wall version: elbows and backs of hands touch the wall in a 'W' shape, lower back gently against the wall.
cues: Slide arms up into a 'Y', then pull elbows down into a 'W'.
Squeeze shoulder blades down and back as you lower.
Ribs down - don't arch to make it look better.
Only go as high as you can keep contact.
mistakes: Arching the lower back away from the wall.
Shrugging shoulders up to the ears.
Forcing hands to touch the wall when mobility isn't there yet.
breathing: Exhale as you slide up, inhale as you pull down.
safety: Wakes up the mid/lower traps and helps posture before pull and push days. A larger chest/upper body can make the back-to-wall version awkward - the facing-the-wall forearm version is just as useful. No pain should be felt in the front of the shoulder.

video.title: Active Physio Works: Scapular Wall Slide

name: Cat-Cow
setup: Use a mat or fold your towel under your knees.
Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, on all fours.
If kneeling is uncomfortable: do it standing with hands on your thighs or on a bench.
cues: Cat: tuck the tailbone, round the back up to the ceiling, chin toward chest.
Cow: let the belly drop, chest forward, gaze slightly up.
Start each movement from the pelvis.
Slow - about one breath each way.
mistakes: Rushing through it.
Only moving the neck instead of the whole spine.
Forcing the end range.
breathing: Inhale into cow (belly down), exhale into cat (back round).
safety: Gentle spinal mobility before deadlift/row/squat days. Keep it pain-free; don't force range if you have back pain. The standing version avoids kneeling on hard floors.

video.title: How to Do a Cat Cow Stretch: A Guide from Physical Therapists

name: Standing Hip Circles
setup: Stand side-on to a machine frame, rack or wall and hold it with one hand for balance.
Stand on the leg closest to the support, slight bend in that knee.
Lift the outside knee to hip height.
cues: Draw big slow circles with the knee: up, out to the side, back, down.
Then reverse direction ('close the gate').
Keep your torso tall and still - only the hip moves.
6-8 each direction, each leg.
mistakes: Leaning the whole body to make the circle bigger.
Going fast and swinging.
Not holding on and losing balance.
breathing: Breathe normally.
safety: Lubricates the hip joint before leg day and squat patterns. Holding a support makes it safe and balanced for a heavier beginner.

video.title: Warm-up Exercise - Hip Circles
video.channel: Live to Move Physical Therapy & Wellness

name: Leg Swings (Front-Back and Side-Side)
setup: Hold a sturdy machine frame or wall with one hand (front-back swings) or both hands (side-to-side swings).
Stand on one leg with a soft knee; the swinging leg hangs relaxed.
Do 10-12 front-back, then turn to face the support and do 10-12 side-to-side. Then switch legs.
cues: Start small, gradually increase the swing.
Torso stays upright - the leg does the moving.
Relaxed, pendulum-like rhythm.
Toes of the standing foot point forward.
mistakes: Kicking up as high as possible from the first rep.
Rounding the back to get the leg higher.
Swinging into people or equipment - check your space.
breathing: Breathe normally, exhale on the forward swing if it helps rhythm.
safety: A dynamic way to loosen hamstrings, hip flexors and groin before leg day. Keep it controlled; ballistic kicks at full range are unnecessary.

video.title: How To Do Leg Swings

name: Bodyweight Squat to Bench
setup: Place a flat bench (or set an adjustable bench flat) on a non-slip floor; a standard bench is about 43-45 cm high - roughly knee height, which is perfect.
Stand in front of it with your heels about 15-30 cm from the bench, feet shoulder-width, toes turned out slightly.
Arms straight out in front for balance.
cues: Sit back and down until your butt lightly touches the bench - don't plop.
Knees push out in line with your toes.
Chest up, whole foot on the floor.
Stand up by driving the floor away; squeeze glutes at the top.
mistakes: Crashing down onto the bench.
Knees caving in.
Heels lifting off the floor.
Rocking forward to get up (use your legs, not momentum).
breathing: Inhale on the way down, exhale as you stand.
safety: Teaches the squat pattern and warms the knees and hips safely - the bench sets a consistent, safe depth for a 95 kg beginner. Never stack loose weight plates on the bench to sit on - they can slide out from under you. If standing up from the bench is too hard at first, just touch it lightly without sitting, or hold the end of the bench/a machine frame for balance. Use as a warm-up before leg day and as a squat-pattern practice.

video.title: Bodyweight Box Squat | Step-by-Step Tutorial

name: World's Greatest Stretch (Supported)
setup: Beginner-friendly version: put your hands on a flat bench instead of the floor.
Face the end of the bench and step one foot forward into a long lunge beside it, back knee down on a folded towel or slightly off the floor.
Place the hand opposite to the front leg on the bench/floor.
cues: Drop the same-side elbow toward the inside of your front foot (only as low as comfortable; with the bench version, toward the inside of the front knee).
Then rotate and reach that arm to the ceiling, eyes following the hand.
Hold each position about 2 seconds, then switch sides.
Keep the back leg long and squeeze its glute.
mistakes: Front knee caving inward.
Rushing through the positions.
Forcing the elbow to the floor - go only as low as is comfortable.
breathing: Exhale as you drop the elbow and as you rotate open.
safety: Opens the hips, hamstrings and upper back in one move - great before leg or pull days. Using a bench for the hands means less bending and more comfort for a heavier body. Difficulty 2 because of balance; hold a support if needed.

video.title: The Worlds GREATEST Stretch

name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Rocks
setup: Face a wall (or the upright of a machine/rack) in a short split stance, front toes about 5-10 cm from the wall.
Hands on the wall for balance.
cues: Keep the front heel glued to the floor.
Drive the knee forward over the middle toes to touch the wall, then back.
Smooth rocks, 10-12 per side.
When it's easy, move the foot slightly further from the wall.
mistakes: Heel lifting.
Knee caving inward instead of tracking over the toes.
Bouncing hard into the end range.
breathing: Breathe normally.
safety: Better ankle mobility makes squats and leg press feel more stable and lets you keep your heels down. Very low stress on the joint - fine for any body weight.

video.title: Knee To Wall Exercise for Ankle Mobility
video.channel: Dr. Jess Harvey, Osteopath & Health Coach

name: Chest Stretch (Doorway or Machine Upright)
setup: Find a doorframe, a sturdy machine upright (e.g. Smith machine or cable column) or a wall corner.
Place your forearm against it with the elbow at about shoulder height and bent 90 degrees ('goalpost' arm).
Stagger your feet, same-side foot forward.
cues: Gently step/turn your body away until you feel a stretch across the chest.
Shoulder down, away from your ear.
Hold 30 s each side, relax and breathe.
Stretch should feel 4-6/10, never painful.
mistakes: Elbow higher than the shoulder (can pinch the shoulder joint).
Twisting so far that the stretch goes into the front of the shoulder joint.
Bouncing.
breathing: Slow, deep breaths; try to relax a little deeper on each exhale.
safety: Ideal cooldown after push days (chest press, shoulder press). If you feel tingling or pinching in the front of the shoulder, lower the elbow. Only use a machine that's not loaded or being used by someone else.

video.title: Doorway Stretch

name: Kneeling Lat Stretch on Bench
setup: Kneel in front of a flat bench on a folded towel or mat.
Place your elbows on the edge of the bench, shoulder-width apart, palms together or holding the towel.
Knees under or slightly behind your hips.
cues: Sit your hips back toward your heels.
Let your chest sink toward the floor between your arms.
Keep the elbows on the bench.
Hold 30-45 s and breathe.
mistakes: Flaring the ribs and over-arching the lower back.
Forcing the chest down so hard it pinches the shoulders.
Holding your breath.
breathing: Breathe deeply into your back; exhale to sink a little lower.
safety: Great after pull days (lat pulldown, rows) and for overhead mobility. If kneeling on the floor hurts, put the towel under the knees or stand and hinge forward with hands on the bench instead.

video.title: The Bench Stretch - The Ultimate Lat and Thoracic Spine Mobility Exercise

name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
setup: Fold your towel under the back knee (or use a mat).
One knee down, the other foot flat in front so both knees are at about 90 degrees.
Hold a bench or machine for balance if needed.
cues: Squeeze the glute of the back leg and tuck the pelvis slightly.
Then shift forward a little - small movement, big stretch.
Stay tall; don't arch the lower back.
Hold 30 s each side.
mistakes: Lunging far forward and arching the back instead of tucking the pelvis.
No towel under the knee on a hard floor.
Letting the front knee cave in.
breathing: Slow breaths; exhale and squeeze the glute a little harder to deepen the stretch.
safety: Hip flexors get tight from long hours sitting in lectures; stretching them helps the lower back and squat. Kneel on something soft - knee pressure is higher at 95 kg.

video.title: Back Exercises to Strengthen and Stretch (Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch) | HSS

name: Lying Hamstring Stretch (Towel)
setup: Lie on your back on a mat (or a flat bench if the floor is busy/dirty).
Bend one knee with the foot flat; loop your towel around the ball of the other foot.
Hold an end of the towel in each hand.
cues: Raise the straight leg until you feel a stretch behind the thigh.
Keep a tiny bend in the knee.
Pull gently with the towel - no yanking.
Hold 30 s each leg; lower back stays relaxed on the floor.
mistakes: Locking the knee hard and feeling it behind the knee rather than the thigh.
Lifting the head and shoulders off the floor.
Bouncing the leg.
breathing: Breathe slowly; on each exhale relax and let the leg come a little closer.
safety: Lying down supports the lower back, which makes this safer than standing toe-touches for a heavier beginner. Good after leg day (leg curls, RDLs, leg press).

video.title: How to do a Lying Hamstring Stretch with Band or Towel

name: Quad Stretch (Foot on Bench)
setup: Stand with your back to a flat bench, about 60-90 cm in front of it.
Rest the top of one foot (laces down) on the bench behind you.
Hold a machine, rack upright or wall beside you for balance.
cues: Stand tall and squeeze the glute of the back leg.
Slightly bend the standing knee to deepen the stretch.
Tuck the pelvis - feel it at the front of the thigh.
Hold 30 s each leg.
mistakes: Arching the lower back.
Standing too close to the bench so the knee is cranked.
Letting the standing knee cave in.
breathing: Breathe slowly and steadily.
safety: Using a bench avoids having to reach back and grab your ankle, which can be hard at 95 kg. Always hold something for balance. Alternative: standing quad stretch holding your ankle with a machine for support.

video.title: Modified Quadriceps Stretch (Foot Resting on a Bench)

name: Wall Calf Stretch
setup: Face a wall or machine upright with both hands on it.
Step one foot back, keeping it straight and the heel on the floor, toes pointing forward.
cues: Lean into the wall until you feel a stretch in the calf of the back leg.
Back heel stays down.
Hold about 30 s straight-knee, then bend the back knee slightly for about 15 s more (targets the lower calf/soleus).
Switch legs.
mistakes: Heel lifting off the floor.
Back foot turned out.
Bouncing.
breathing: Breathe steadily.
safety: Essential after incline walking and leg day - calves and Achilles take a lot of load at 95 kg. Ease into it.

video.title: Standing Calf Stretch (HSS)

name: Figure-4 Glute Stretch
setup: Lie on your back on a mat with both knees bent, feet flat.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee to make a '4' shape.
Seated alternative (easier if lying is uncomfortable): sit tall on a flat bench, cross the ankle over the knee and hinge forward with a flat back.
cues: Reach through and hold behind the bottom thigh.
Gently pull that thigh toward your chest.
Push the top knee slightly away.
Hold 30 s each side, head relaxed on the floor.
mistakes: Lifting the head and straining the neck.
Rounding the back hard in the seated version.
Pulling so hard the knee hurts.
breathing: Slow, deep breaths.
safety: Releases the glutes and outer hip after leg day and squats. If pulling the leg in is hard because of the belly, use the seated-on-bench version - it works the same muscles. Should never be felt in the knee.

video.title: Piriformis Figure 4 Stretch - Ask Doctor Jo

name: Child's Pose
setup: Kneel on a mat or towel, big toes together and knees wide (wider knees = more room for the belly).
Sit hips back toward heels and walk your hands forward.
If the floor is uncomfortable, put your forearms on a flat bench instead.
cues: Let your chest sink toward the floor.
Forehead down or rest on your hands.
Reach long through the arms.
Breathe into your back for 30-60 s.
mistakes: Knees together, which squashes the stomach and limits the stretch.
Forcing the hips down onto the heels.
Shrugging shoulders.
breathing: Slow deep belly breathing - inhale through the nose, long exhale.
safety: A relaxing end to every session; eases the lower back. Wide knees and a cushion under the hips or knees make it comfortable for a heavier beginner. Skip or use the bench version if knees complain.

video.title: How to do a Child's Pose Stretch | Proper Form & Technique | NASM

name: Calf Raise Machine

startingWeightKg.note: This is the machine listed as the 'Ankle machine' at the UG gym. Stack numbers differ between brands, so treat the number as a pin setting. Standing machine: start where 15 slow, full-range reps feel steady. Seated machine (plates on a lever over your knees): log only the plates you add and start with 10-20 kg.

setup: Check which kind it is. Standing: pads rest on your shoulders. Seated: a pad rests on top of your thighs just above the knees.
Standing: set the shoulder pads so you have to bend your knees slightly to get under them, then stand up tall to lift the weight off the stack.
Seated: set the thigh pad so it presses lightly on your lower thighs, then push up on your toes and release the safety lever.
Put only the balls of your feet on the edge of the step, hip-width apart, toes pointing forward. Heels hang off.
Hold the handles lightly for balance. Wipe the step dry if it is sweaty.
cues: Let your heels sink below the step for a deep stretch, pause 1-2 seconds
Push through the big toe and rise as high as you can
Squeeze at the top for 1 second
Slow on the way down, no bouncing
Knees stay still: only the ankles move
mistakes: Bouncing at the bottom instead of pausing
Tiny half reps with heavy weight
Bending and straightening the knees to help (standing version)
Rolling onto the outside edges of the feet
breathing: Breathe out as you rise, breathe in as you lower. Keep breathing steadily for the whole set.
safety: A very safe machine for a beginner. The main risk is a foot slipping off a wet step, so use dry shoes, keep the whole ball of each foot on the step and re-engage the safety lever (seated) before you step off. On the standing version, do not round your back under the pads; stand tall. Calves get very sore after the first sessions, so keep week 1 easy.

name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift

startingWeightKg.note: Total weight including the 20 kg bar. A good first guess is 1.6-1.8x the per-hand weight you use on the dumbbell RDL (e.g. 2 x 16 kg dumbbells -> about 26-30 kg on the bar). Only used from Phase 3 (week 9) after 8 weeks of dumbbell RDLs.

setup: There is no rack at the UG gym, so this lift starts from the floor. Load the largest-diameter plates you can (20 kg plates if your total allows) so the bar sits around mid-shin. If only small plates fit your load and the bar sits very low, do the dumbbell RDL instead.
Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet, feet hip-width apart, toes forward.
Get the bar to standing safely: bend your knees, grip just outside your legs with palms facing you, flat back, chest up, then stand up by pushing the floor away. This pick-up is not a rep.
Stand tall with the bar against your thighs, soft knees, shoulders back and down.
Put the bar back down the same way at the end of the set: bend the knees and keep your back flat.
cues: Push your hips back like closing a car door with your butt
Bar slides down your thighs, stays touching your legs
Flat back: stop when your hamstrings are tight, usually just below the knees to mid-shin
Squeeze your glutes to stand up tall
Do not lean back at the top
mistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach lower
Bending the knees more and more so it turns into a squat
Letting the bar drift forward away from the legs
Rushing the lowering phase or bouncing at the bottom
Picking the bar up from the floor with a rounded back
breathing: Breathe in and brace your stomach at the top, keep the brace while you hinge down, breathe out as you stand up. Do not hold your breath for several reps in a row.
safety: Range of motion ends where your back would start to round, not where the bar touches the floor. Start light and add weight only when every rep looks the same. If you feel it in your lower back rather than your hamstrings, lighten the load and push the hips further back. Stop with any sharp back pain and switch to the dumbbell RDL or cable pull-through.

video.title: How to do the ROMANIAN DEADLIFT! | 2 Minute Tutorial

name: Bodyweight Good Morning (Hip Hinge Drill)
setup: No weight at all. The pictures show a bar on the back: ignore the bar, you only copy the body position.
Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent.
Put your hands on your hips, or cross them over your chest. Do not pull on your neck.
cues: Push your hips back to touch an imaginary wall behind you
Keep your back long and flat, chest proud
Go down slowly (about 3 seconds) until you feel the backs of your legs stretch
Squeeze your glutes to stand up
mistakes: Bending the knees a lot so it becomes a squat
Rounding the back to go lower
Looking straight up and cranking the neck
breathing: Breathe in on the way down, breathe out as you stand up.
safety: This drill teaches the hip hinge you use in Romanian deadlifts, so do it slowly and stop the moment your lower back starts to round. Stop if you feel pain in the back rather than a stretch in the hamstrings.

video.title: Bodyweight Good Morning (Hip Hinge)

name: Scapular Pulldown (Straight Arms)

startingWeightKg.note: Light: about half of what you use for lat pulldowns, just enough to pull your arms fully overhead. This is a warm-up, not a working set.

setup: Sit at the lat pulldown with your thighs under the pad, same as a normal pulldown.
Take the bar with a shoulder-width or slightly wider grip, arms straight.
Let the weight pull your shoulders up toward your ears. This is the start position. The pictures show the same movement on a pull-up bar.
cues: Arms stay straight the whole time
Pull your shoulders down away from your ears
Hold 1 second with shoulder blades down, then let them rise slowly
Small movement: a few centimetres is correct
mistakes: Bending the elbows so it becomes a light pulldown
Leaning back to move the bar
Using so much weight that the movement disappears
breathing: Breathe out as you pull the shoulders down, breathe in as they rise.
safety: Very low risk. It wakes up the muscles that hold your shoulder blades in place before pulling. If the pulldown is busy, do scapular wall slides instead.

video.title: Scapular Pull Down
video.channel: Revo Physiotherapy and Sports Performance Denver

name: Seated Dumbbell Lateral Raise

startingWeightKg.note: Per dumbbell. Sitting removes body swing, so start lighter than you think: 15 smooth reps with 2-3 left.

setup: Sit on the end of a flat bench (or an upright seat), feet flat and a little apart.
Hold a light dumbbell in each hand by your sides, palms facing in, elbows slightly bent.
Sit tall: chest up, shoulders down away from your ears.
cues: Lead with the elbows, not the hands
Raise out to the sides until the arms are level with the shoulders
Pinkies level with or slightly above the thumbs, never higher
Lower slowly over 2 seconds
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears
Leaning back or rocking to swing the weight
Lifting above shoulder height
Going too heavy and turning it into a front raise
breathing: Breathe out as you raise, breathe in as you lower.
safety: Very low risk. If the front of the shoulder pinches, raise slightly forward of the body (about 20-30 degrees) and stop at shoulder height.

name: Head-Supported Dumbbell Rear Delt Raise
aliases: Bent Over Rear Delt Raise With Head On Bench
Rear Delt Raise Head on Bench

startingWeightKg.note: Per dumbbell. Rear delts are small: start very light and use 15-20 controlled reps.

setup: Set an adjustable bench to a high incline and stand behind it.
Hinge forward until your forehead rests on the top of the backrest; back flat, knees soft.
Let a light dumbbell hang in each hand under your shoulders, palms facing each other.
cues: Keep the forehead on the bench the whole set
Sweep the arms out wide, like spreading wings
Stop when the arms are in line with the body
Lower slowly; do not let the weights clank
mistakes: Lifting the head off the bench and standing up
Squeezing the shoulder blades hard so the back does the work
Bending the elbows more and more to row the weight
Using weights that are too heavy
breathing: Breathe out as you raise the arms, breathe in as you lower them.
safety: The head support takes load off the lower back, which is why it suits beginners and anyone with back niggles. Set the bench so you do not have to round your back to reach it.

name: Diverging Lat Pulldown (Machine)

startingWeightKg.note: Log the total weight you move: the pin number on a stack machine, or all the plates on both arms if it is plate-loaded. Start light; you should hit 12 clean reps with 2-3 left in the tank.

setup: Set the seat so the handles are just within reach with your arms fully straight overhead.
Set the thigh pad so it presses firmly on top of your thighs with feet flat on the floor - you should not lift off the seat when you pull.
Grab one handle in each hand (neutral or overhand, whichever handles the machine has), chest up, slight lean back.
cues: Drive your elbows down and out, then in to your sides
Let the handles travel in their arc - don't fight the machine
Squeeze your lats for 1 second at the bottom
Control it up for 2-3 seconds and feel the stretch at the top
mistakes: Leaning far back and turning it into a row
Yanking with body swing to move too much weight
Stopping halfway up instead of getting a full stretch
Letting one arm do more work than the other
breathing: Breathe in at the top with arms straight; exhale as you pull the handles down.
safety: Seated and supported, so it is shoulder- and back-friendly. Each arm moves on its own, which shows up a weaker side - match the reps on both. Return the handles to the top under control before standing up; don't let them fly up. Wipe the handles and your palms before each set so your grip doesn't slip.
